# Curity audit-source companion

This source extension retains original Curity audit exports beside the existing SF74 case system. It supplies exact source interpretation, review and comparison. The existing OAuth verifier, observer, SF93 incident engine and SF74 store continue to own their original operations.

Commercial source: Commons cc3e990aa3f9129ca0b027ff608343369121e81e, opportunities/curity_oauth_support_2026. Original operation: DBC61-CURITY-OAUTH-SUPPORT-WORKSHARE-20261013. Supplier relationship, message 1a132c76382757f9 and commercial decisions remain with their existing owner.

## Runtime and source limits

Node 22 or later, built-in modules only. The native commissioning programme uses its selected complete existing host. No package installation or service starts occur on importing these modules.

A selection contains at most 20 original files, one million nonblank framed records and one GiB of complete original source. A single parsed record is bounded to eight MiB. Every oversized or malformed range still points to its complete retained original; it remains unclassifiable and makes the source incomplete. JSON framing failures retain the entire unclassifiable remainder, whose internal record count is unknown. Counts describe observed framing, not a guessed number of events inside malformed bytes.

Original input and reports stream to disk. The identity index holds one entry for each distinct installation/event ID and each distinct content variant; select native memory for that cardinality, potentially hundreds of MiB for a million events. This is not a constant-memory claim. Reports and UI pages remain bounded. At most 1,000 exact occurrences can be selected into a case review; all other source records remain in the companion and paginated reports.

## Build and review

Import from source.mjs:

- buildEdition(input) resolves the complete immutable manifest after original retention, framing, mapping, accounting and publication.
- openEdition(directory, {verify:true}) reads the same manifest and checks every declared file, mapping and review.
- readEventPage(directory, {after:0, limit:100}) and readFindingPage use sparse byte indexes. They return {items,nextAfter,total,editionId}; after is a zero-based report-row cursor, not an original file ordinal.
- readSourceRecord(directory, ref) returns the exact Buffer and digest for a bounded original byte range.
- compareSourceEditions(beforeDirectory,afterDirectory,{directory}) streams the complete classifiable event identity/content/occurrence comparison into changes.jsonl plus comparison.json. It includes both complete source manifests' file changes and original findings identities; unknown events inside malformed bytes are not assigned invented IDs. This is the full-source comparison alongside the bounded reviewed-selection comparison.
- editionFiles(directory) returns {manifest,files}, adding the original manifest.json identity to the complete portable member list.

The complete input is:

    {
      directory: "/private/owned/editions/inspection-01",
      installationId: "the-selected-installation",
      sourceContext: "SUPPLIER_EXPORT",
      sourceEdition: "supplier-export-identifier",
      files: [{
        path: "/private/received/original.ndjson",
        name: "original.ndjson",
        format: "ndjson",
        sha256: "<actual original digest>",
        sourceUri: "<retained source locator>",
        exportId: "<actual export identity>",
        metadata: {}
      }],
      mapping: { ... },
      coverage: {profiles: [], listeners: [], ...actualCoverageMetadata},
      binding: { ... },
      review: {
        confirmed: false, operator: null, reason: null,
        decisions: [], selection: []
      }
    }

sourceContext is exactly PUBLISHER_EXAMPLE or SUPPLIER_EXPORT. A documentation example cannot become a supplier result by choosing another label. The supplied sourceEdition remains stable across an inspection and its reviewed edition.

Input files receive sourceId values source-1, source-2 and so on in selected order. Original name, URI, export identity and metadata are preserved. Identical full files can appear twice; their separate source IDs retain both supplied occurrences. The original bytes are deduplicated only within that edition's originals/<sha256>.bin storage.

The destination must be new. A private .building-<process>-<random> sibling retains interrupted work and never advertises a complete edition. If acknowledgment is lost after publication, open the original destination; do not build over it. Only the owner may retire an interrupted private staging directory after reconciling the same operation.

For review, inspect pages first, then build a new destination from the same retained original paths and expected hashes. Select the exact previous sourceEdition, coverage and binding; edit the mapping only as an explicit new revision. Review decisions are:

    {
      confirmed: true,
      operator: "named reviewer",
      reason: "scope and mapping decision",
      decisions: [{
        sourceId: "source-1",
        recordOrdinal: 1,
        action: "accept-collision",
        reason: "decision about this exact occurrence"
      }],
      selection: [{sourceId: "source-1", recordOrdinal: 1}]
    }

Actions are include, exclude or accept-collision. An include cannot silently override a collision or move an event outside the selected window. An excluded malformed record remains an incomplete source. Decisions naming missing records fail the build. Review IDs derive from complete review content.

## Explicit layouts

Structured fields use:

    {
      schema: "curity.audit-mapping/v1",
      layout: "fields",
      contentPath: ["audit"],
      fields: {
        type: ["audit","type"], id: ["audit","id"],
        instant: ["audit","instant"], message: ["message"],
        client: ["audit","client"], subject: ["audit","subject"]
      },
      outerTimestamp: {path:["eventTime"], unit:"literal-only"}
    }

Every field keeps absent, null, empty and supplied values distinct. Strings retain their actual decoded value; numbers retain their original lexeme, including values beyond JavaScript integer precision. Nested mapped values retain canonical lossless JSON. Complete original JSON bytes remain authoritative. Duplicate JSON object member names are ambiguous and remain findings.

The four mandatory audit fields type, id, instant and message must be text. Type and ID must be nonempty; an empty message is valid because the published structured example contains one. Optional mapping paths must be explicitly selected. Unknown event types are retained rather than filtered by an outdated hard-coded list.

JSONLayout with the documented textual audit envelope uses:

    {
      schema:"curity.audit-mapping/v1",
      layout:"curity-message",
      messagePath:["message"],
      outerTimestamp:{path:["timeMillis"],unit:"literal-only"}
    }

This selects a strict text grammar: event type, bracketed event ID and named quoted attributes, followed by message text. Quote and backslash escapes are recognized. Other escape conventions or ambiguous delimiters remain findings until the actual export contract selects a supported parser. The extension does not guess a structured layout from a familiar field name.

The outer timestamp unit must be seconds, milliseconds, microseconds, nanoseconds or literal-only. It is retained separately and never replaces event instant. Even a field named timeMillis does not establish its unit.

## Exact time, identity and coverage

Event instant is an explicit RFC3339 string with timezone. Its original literal and arbitrarily long fraction survive interpretation. Event-time ordering compares integer seconds and padded fractional digits, independently of source order. Invalid calendar values, leap-second representations and unknown -00:00 offsets remain unclassifiable; they are never silently normalized.

The selected window is start-inclusive, end-exclusive:

    binding: {
      installationId: "the-selected-installation",
      resourceId: "the-existing-resource",
      configurationHash: "<actual reviewed configuration SHA256>",
      window: {start: "<RFC3339>", end: "<RFC3339>"},
      observation: null
    }

An optional observation is a retained aggregate source link:

    {
      sha256: "<actual observation-file digest>",
      configurationHash: "<same reviewed configuration>",
      endpoint: "<original selected endpoint>",
      stages: ["authentication","authorization","hostAuthority","jwks"],
      window: {start:"<actual observation start>",end:"<actual observation end>"}
    }

It is a reviewed association of configuration, resource and windows. No subject, request, client or token is derived from redacted minute counters. Windows may differ and remain explicit. Never sum overlapping aggregate windows or interpret matching timestamps as a one-to-one request join.

Listener/profile coverage records actual supplied configuration and export declarations. The manifest explicitly labels this CONFIGURATION_AND_EXPORT_DECLARATION_ONLY; configuration is not proof that all relevant events arrived.

Event identity is SHA256 of the selected installation and original event ID. Content identity preserves selected original event content and typed mapped fields. Same identity/content is a repeat with every occurrence retained. Different content under the same ID is a collision. The identity index retains all variants and counts. Source order does not elect an authoritative winner. A later variant also makes an earlier selected occurrence ambiguous unless the review explicitly accepts that occurrence.

## Manifest and reference contract

The immutable manifest schema is curity.audit-edition/v1. Its id hashes the full manifest body excluding id. It carries sourceFiles, files, mappingRevision, configurationHash, binding, coverage, counts, optionalCoverage, eventTimeSpan, sourceContext and state COMPLETE or INCOMPLETE_SOURCE.

counts.dispositions reconciles exactly to sourceRecords. classifiable plus unclassifiable also reconciles. Other counts describe parallel dimensions such as scope and review, and should not be added as if mutually exclusive.

The full closure is:

- manifest.json
- originals/<each exact digest>.bin
- events.jsonl and findings.jsonl
- indexes/identities.jsonl and indexes/pages.json
- mapping.json and review.json

The manifest files list covers every member except itself; editionFiles adds its exact identity for wrapping and transfer. No sender absolute input path is required by a recipient.

References carry editionId, sourceId, fileSha256, recordOrdinal, byteStart, byteEnd, eventId, eventKey, contentSha256, mappingRevision and disposition. Byte ranges are zero-based start-inclusive/end-exclusive in the original file. File ordinals include NDJSON blank lines; report-row cursors do not.

Review functions:

- validateReviewedEdition(manifest) returns that manifest or throws. It requires a confirmed named review and 1–1,000 classified, resolved evidence selections. Source completeness remains a separate visible status.
- selectedEventReferences(manifest) returns the exact references with editionId attached.
- reviewedSelection(manifest,{editionId,reviewId,eventKeys}) returns schema curity.reviewed-selection/v1 with events and the frozen source/configuration context.
- compareEditions(before,after) compares reviewed selections and flags identity/content, source occurrence, mapping, configuration and coverage changes. Its scope is explicitly REVIEWED_SELECTION, not a claim to compare every audit record.
- compareReturn(manifest,actual) compares per-event returned source bindings and files. It preserves the actual return source identity and reports every omitted, unexpected, repeated or changed selected occurrence.

A returned envelope contains kind per-event or bulk-acknowledgment, sourceReturn {sha256,bytes}, editionId, reviewId, case {id,revision} and optional events. Each per-event entry contains sourceRef, disposition, targetId, caseId, caseRevision and files [{sha256,bytes}]. A bulk acknowledgment remains UNVERIFIED_DETAIL; it never demonstrates per-event preservation or invents target event IDs. The SF74 case has no synthetic per-audit-event table, so its actual package comparison may truthfully lack target event IDs while proving complete companion hashes.

The all-source comparison also compares complete original-file descriptors, including source occurrence/order, framing and metadata. A repeated or empty original file is retained as a distinct source occurrence even when its storage bytes are shared; descriptor changes remain visible in addedFiles and removedFiles.

## Complete comparison recovery

compareSourceEditions(beforeDirectory, afterDirectory, {directory}) verifies both complete source editions before work or completed-result reuse. Each new sibling .building attempt retains INPUT.json with both exact manifest hashes, source edition IDs, installation and comparison scope before it writes changes. Output is published by one directory rename only after changes.jsonl and comparison.json are complete.

A lost process or acknowledgment can be continued with the same call and exact sources. If the final directory is absent, a fresh attempt computes the same comparison and preserves prior interrupted siblings. If the final directory is present, the function verifies its comparison identity, selection, fixed changes filename, full changes bytes and retained request, then returns the existing result. A concurrent completed publisher is received through those same checks. Historical completed comparison directories without INPUT.json remain readable after full result and source verification.

An existing final directory without comparison.json is not a normal partial publication from this producer. It is retained and reported for inspection; the function never deletes it or overwrites unrelated or damaged files. Partial attempt siblings may be retired only through their original owner's ordinary retained-artifact workflow after the completed result is preserved.

## Existing case and portable receiving

The Curity bridge uses SF74's original CaseStore revisions, artifact retention and native source-package receiver. It never inserts an arbitrary seventh source slot. The full audit edition remains a provider companion bound to the existing case, incident/source identities and reviewed selection.

Case changes are explicit and revision guarded. Following edits compare the accepted baseline to fresh staff state. Rollback changes only still-matching selected fields, preserving other staff work. Receiving uses the native returned case ID and revision. Imported incident bindings remain passive until the recipient selects the local original service.

The operator, case bridge and portable receiver are documented in OPERATOR.md. The complete original-service commissioning programme is documented in COMMISSIONING.md.

## Publisher example and actual acceptance

publisher-inputs.json transcribes the two original examples in Curity's Logging Best Practices page. Field values are exact; JSON formatting is our retained source representation, not a claim that original HTTP response bytes were acquired. It is labeled PUBLISHER_EXAMPLE throughout.

Original primary sources:
- https://curity.io/resources/learn/logging-best-practices/
- https://curity.io/docs/identity-server/system-and-operation/operation-and-monitoring/audit-logging/
- https://curity.io/docs/identity-server/facilities/event-listeners/

Source interpretation, worked publisher execution, installed supplier execution and commercial acceptance remain distinct. No customer log, Curity installation, payment, award or customer acceptance is established by these source files.

# Curity audit review in the original Support desk

This extension retains complete Curity JSON or NDJSON source, exact mapping and named review, then attaches a bounded evidence selection to an existing SF74 case. The original merchant workspace, native incident API, case writer and complete-case receiver remain authoritative.

## Open the selected complete application

Use the complete original merchant source closure with the provider extension joined into sf74-merchant-support-console/server.mjs. Open it with the existing Node and Python dependencies used by SF74; no new identity provider is installed.

Create an operator-owned mode-0600 configuration file in a private directory:

```json
{
  "casesDir": "/absolute/private/original-cases",
  "directory": "/absolute/private/curity-companion",
  "sourceDir": "/absolute/private/original-source-delivery",
  "applicationFiles": [
    {
      "name": "repo-relative/path/to/each-actual-source-file",
      "path": "/absolute/selected/source/file",
      "bytes": 123,
      "sha256": "ACTUAL_SHA256_OF_THAT_COMPLETE_FILE"
    }
  ],
  "port": 0
}
```

The example inventory is a shape, not a usable source receipt. Supply every file from the selected readable application closure with actual byte counts and hashes. Package export verifies every file. Keep the companion directory outside the cases directory and its original source-delivery directory. Existing handoffSources and incidentSources configuration paths can be selected explicitly; credentials remain under the original host configuration.

Run:

```sh
node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf74-merchant-support-console/curity/http.mjs --config /absolute/private/curity-config.json
```

Open the returned local /curity/ URL. The original server keeps its loopback and exact Host checks. Private reads reject foreign origins and every mutation requires the original same-origin browser. The provider handler finishes its active requests before the original underlying case/source/incident services close.

For embedding in the maintained native programme, import startCurityConsole from http.mjs. It returns the original server/url/close result and providerExtension.controller. The controller factory is openCurityOperator({directory,store,casesDirectory,sourceDelivery,incidentDesk,applicationFiles,python,environment}).

## 1. Retain the original source

Choose 1–20 actual original files, at most one GiB in total (including empty originals), and explicitly choose JSON document or NDJSON framing for each. Original filenames, file order and SHA-256 remain attached to the immutable edition. Identical files supplied twice retain distinct source-N occurrence identities.

Choose PUBLISHER_EXAMPLE for published examples. This label remains visible in the review, case evidence and portable package. Choose SUPPLIER_EXPORT only for an actual supplied installation export. Enter the actual installation, source edition, resource, configuration SHA-256 and exact RFC3339 window. Profile/listener coverage is explicit; absence is not inferred coverage.

Map exact field paths or select the strict Curity message layout. Type, ID, audit instant and message remain lossless: large numeric identifiers and nanosecond instants are not rounded; missing and empty fields remain distinct. Outer timestamps have an independently selected unit and never silently replace the audit instant.

An optional observer descriptor must refer to actual retained configuration/window-bound evidence. Audit events are not joined to individual requests or OAuth minute counters. Original OAuth credentials, counters and issuer behavior stay in the original observer.

The initial build is an unconfirmed inspection edition. The browser saves the request identity before dispatch; failed acknowledgments can be retried with the same body. An interrupted upload accepts only the original matching prefix. After reopening, reselect the same full files and framing to finish the retained intake. Different bytes are preserved as a conflict, never substituted.

## 2. Inspect and confirm a review

Read paged events and findings. Each event shows its typed fields, exact audit instant, source file and original record ordinal. “Read original” returns the exact original record bytes and verifies their SHA-256. Complete original downloads are available for records beyond the bounded preview size.

Select exact source occurrences. Include/exclude decisions and an explicit reason for an accepted collision remain attached to the original sourceId and recordOrdinal. A later colliding variant can change a previously seen event's final disposition; the confirmed immutable review, not a stale page row, controls case attachment.

Enter the named operator and review reason, then freeze a new confirmed edition. The original inspection remains. It uses the same complete original files and source edition. Source mappings are not changed silently. INCOMPLETE_SOURCE remains visibly incomplete even when classified evidence is explicitly reviewed. Only accepted, repeated or explicitly accepted collision occurrences can enter the confirmed case selection.

At most 1,000 references are attached to a case operation. The complete audit remains pageable and is included in the handover.

## 3. Apply evidence to the existing case

Read the existing native case and its current revision. Choose evidence from a confirmed review, add a case note and select only the metadata changes intended. The metadata status choices come from the native case API.

“Prepare case comparison” freezes the source/review identity, exact input, native beforeimage and proposed field changes. Review that saved plan before applying. The writer rechecks the original case revision. If staff changed it, prepare a new reviewed operation from the current case.

A lost save acknowledgment is reconciled through the original native revision history. Repeating an applied operation returns its original receipt and a fresh comparison; it does not create another case or overwrite later work.

The comparison shows the accepted value, current value and whether each selected field is still unchanged. “Restore this operation's unchanged fields” requires a fresh current revision. It restores only those selected fields while preserving current workspace/support bytes and unrelated metadata. A staff-changed selected field is skipped and reported; other still-matching fields are restored. Fields already at their before-value are reported separately as already restored. Original evidence, beforeimages, receipts and native history remain retained.

An optional incident acknowledgment is a separate explicit action against the original source ID, incident ID, configuration and revision. It does not send notifications, change OAuth configuration or reverse a real acknowledgment during case rollback. Received packages cannot inherit authority to acknowledge the sender's incident.

## 4. Export and receive the complete package

Build a package for an applied operation. It contains:

- The complete unchanged native case package and its history, original source bundles and receiving information.
- Every original audit file, event/finding report, mapping, review and exact manifest.
- The case operation's selection, beforeimages, original application receipt and available rollback/acknowledgment history.
- The complete selected readable application source inventory.

The export freezes its source/case/application selection and creation time before copying. Interrupted copies resume only an exact prefix. A different existing member is preserved. The final manifest is published only after every declared original member exists. Repeating the same export ID reopens that complete package.

“Save complete package folder” uses the browser directory API where available. Existing different files are preserved. The fallback lists every member with its required relative path. A manifest alone is not a complete handover. An operator can also copy the complete retained packages/exports/EXPORT_ID directory through the native filesystem or the existing delivery mechanism.

For a receiving workspace, open an independent original SF74 case store and source delivery, then select the whole exported folder. Uploading the manifest never authorizes arbitrary local paths: only declared original member names are accepted. Every byte count/hash, audit edition, review, native package and application inventory is verified before receiving.

The unchanged native receiver creates its actual recipient case UUID and imported revision. The companion records that original local baseline and source identity. It does not invent a local pre-import case. Subsequent staff edits are preserved when the same package is received again; the first receiving receipt remains the completed boundary. The received source remains pageable and exact. Selective rollback on a received binding compares current native fields with the actual accepted baseline.

Receiving source does not activate or execute imported application files or acquire sender credentials. To run the application, explicitly select its complete readable source and original dependencies as a normal local programme.

## Direct interfaces

- controller.prepareSource(input), uploadSource({inputId,index,stream}), buildSource({inputId}).
- controller.freezeReview({inputId,sourceInputId,review,mapping?}), then buildSource on that new input.
- controller.source.catalog(), manifest(editionId), events/findings({editionId,after,limit}), original({editionId,ref}), reviewedSelection({editionId,reviewId,eventKeys}).
- controller.bridge.prepare(input), apply({operationId}), compare({operationId}), rollback({operationId,rollbackId,expectedRevision,actor}), acknowledge({operationId,by,notes}).
- controller.portable.exportPackage({operationId,exportId}).
- controller.portable.receive({packageDirectory,expectedManifestSha256,requestId,actor,receivingDirectory,...explicit native receiving stores when different}).

The full source/parser contract is in SOURCE.md. The actual complete observer, case, staff-edit and independent receiving programme is in COMMISSIONING.md; its real result distinguishes source verification from executed native outcomes. This guide itself does not claim an executed customer installation.

## Whole case history and recipient return

An export selects and freezes the actual current native case revision, including intervening staff edits. The attachment's accepted revision and original field beforeimages remain separate. The original SF74 package carries the complete native case history. The companion carries every relevant Curity operation's plan and receipts, all referenced immutable audit editions, and retained received history. Historical operation paths include the original case UUID and operation ID, so separate cases never collapse matching operation names.

Receiving restores every referenced audit edition into the recipient's source catalog. It creates one local active binding for the selected operation at the actual imported native baseline. Earlier operations and incident bindings remain historical; they do not register or acknowledge the sender's incident service. Re-export carries that received history plus local operations and the recipient's current case. A later rollback restores only fields still equal to the accepted after-values; each changed staff field is reported under skipped, while restored lists the fields actually restored. The current revision remains the race guard.

## Original OAuth resource intake
